headline: Highest risk is medium: Argo Workflows can egress allowlisted data while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, creating limited but real leakage and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a can call REST/GRPC APIs and has allowlisted egress, but agent_b has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, MCP, or network surfaces. With no bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate runtimes with no shared IPC.
Do not wire agent_b outputs into agent_a prompts automatically.
Add provenance tags if any shared channel is introduced.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization on any future bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted network egress, so it can transmit data it processes. agent_b is documentation-only with no filesystem read or network egress, so it is unlikely to leak data itself. The pair still creates a default leakage path if sensitive artifacts flow into agent_a and are then sent onward.
conditions: IF sensitive artifacts or parameters are supplied to agent_a, THEN those contents may leave the local environment via allowlisted egress.
IF agent_b is later connected to shared files or stdin, THEN leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict agent_a inputs to non-sensitive test data.
Review allowlist destinations before each run.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows.
Log outbound requests from agent_a for spot checks.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no filesystem-write, git, or shell capabilities listed, and agent_b explicitly lacks write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and supports_multiple_instances. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so a write-write conflict pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, THEN conflict risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared assets.
Avoid mounting a common writable workspace.
Do not grant git mutation scopes to either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can produce workflow outputs, but agent_b is a cheatsheet/documentation agent with no action-taking or API surfaces, so it is not positioned to blindly execute A's results. The main risk is limited to misrendered or over-trusted text if outputs are manually copied, which is a small blast radius.
conditions: IF a human manually copies agent_a output into agent_b as authoritative text, THEN cascading error becomes possible.
IF agent_b is repurposed to generate downstream actions, THEN severity increases.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing agent_a outputs.
Label agent_a outputs as unverified.
Keep agent_b in documentation-only mode.
Use a checklist for any copied facts.
requires-engineering: add validation between generation and reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, residency, or retention commitments exposed. agent_a touches artifacts and parameters, while agent_b touches no data classes and has no storage or network surfaces. The pair shows only a small compliance gap because no regulated-data pathway is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_a's artifacts or parameters, THEN compliance review is required.
IF either profile is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, THEN this verdict may understate risk.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention for any artifacts processed by agent_a.
Confirm deployment region before use.
Avoid storing outputs in long-lived logs.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
